# select_aws_connection (Resource)

A connection to one AWS account: the S3 location AWS delivers its Cost and Usage Report to, and how SELECT signs in to read it, either by assuming a role in the account or with an IAM user's access key.

## About

An AWS connection is how SELECT reads one AWS account's spend: the S3 bucket AWS delivers that account's Cost and Usage Report to, the path within it the report lands under, and how SELECT signs in to read those objects. To learn more, see the [SELECT documentation](https://select.dev/docs/getting-started).

This resource is backed by SELECT's v2 API, where the underlying resource is called an AWS account and lives at `/v2/aws-accounts`. The `api_key` configured on the provider must carry the `aws_accounts:read` and `aws_accounts:write` scopes; without them every operation fails with an authorization error.

## Example Usage

```terraform
# SELECT reads an AWS account's spend out of the Cost and Usage Report AWS
# delivers to S3. Here it assumes a role in the account that can list and read
# the report objects under the prefix. The role's trust policy names SELECT's
# AWS account, with the external ID shown in SELECT as the sts:ExternalId
# condition.
resource "select_aws_connection" "production" {
  name = "Acme Production"

  aws_account_id = "123456789012"
  s3_bucket      = "acme-cost-and-usage-reports"
  s3_prefix      = "cur/production"
  region         = "us-east-1"

  credentials = {
    authentication_method = "role"
    role_arn              = "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/select-cur-read"
  }
}

# A report delivered to the root of its bucket has no prefix. Omit s3_prefix
# rather than setting it to "", which SELECT stores as an empty prefix rather
# than as no prefix at all.
resource "select_aws_connection" "sandbox" {
  name = "Acme Sandbox"

  aws_account_id = "210987654321"
  s3_bucket      = "acme-sandbox-cur"
  region         = "eu-west-1"

  # An IAM user's access key pair works too, with the same read access.
  credentials = {
    authentication_method = "access_key"
    access_key_id         = var.aws_sandbox_access_key_id
    secret_access_key     = var.aws_sandbox_secret_access_key
  }

  # Hold off syncing until the connection has been reviewed.
  sync_enabled = false
}
```

## Schema

### Required

- `aws_account_id` (String) The 12-digit id of the AWS account that created the Cost and Usage Report export: the payer account, or a member account exporting its own usage.
- `credentials` (Attributes) The IAM user SELECT authenticates as when it reads the Cost and Usage Report. The secret in this block is stored in a secret store and never returned by the API, so SELECT cannot detect changes made to it outside Terraform. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--credentials))
- `name` (String) Display name for the account, as shown throughout SELECT.
- `region` (String) The AWS region the bucket is in, such as `us-east-1`. SELECT reads the bucket through this region's S3 endpoint.
- `s3_bucket` (String) The S3 bucket AWS delivers this account's Cost and Usage Report to.

### Optional

- `s3_prefix` (String) Path within the bucket that the report is delivered under. Null when the report is delivered at the root of the bucket.
- `sync_enabled` (Boolean) Whether SELECT starts syncing data for this account.

### Read-Only

- `added_by_email` (String) Email address of the person who added the account. Null when it was not added by a person.
- `connection_id` (String) Identifier of the underlying connection, which SELECT reports sync state and connection alerts against.
- `create_time` (String) When the account was added.
- `etag` (String) Opaque strong ETag for this connection. Sent as `If-Match` on updates and deletes so a change made outside Terraform cannot be silently overwritten.
- `id` (String) The connection's identifier in SELECT, assigned when it is added. Use it with `terraform import` to bring an existing connection under management.
- `last_successful_sync_time` (String) When SELECT last completed a sync for this account. Null before the first one succeeds.
- `update_time` (String) When the account was last changed.

<a id="nestedatt--credentials"></a>
### Nested Schema for `credentials`

Required:

- `authentication_method` (String) How SELECT signs in to read this account's report.

Optional:

- `access_key_id` (String) Access key id of the IAM user SELECT authenticates as. Required for `access_key`.
- `role_arn` (String) ARN of the role SELECT assumes. Required for `role`.
- `secret_access_key` (String, Sensitive) Secret access key paired with `access_key_id`. Required for `access_key`.

## Import

`select_aws_connection` can be imported using the connection's ID in SELECT:

```bash
terraform import select_aws_connection.example 2f1c8b4e-9a6d-4d1f-9d0e-7d3a5b6c8e01
```

The ID is assigned by SELECT when the connection is added, so unlike a Snowflake account there is nothing about your AWS setup that predicts it. It is the `id` attribute, and it is also the last path segment of the connection's page in the SELECT UI.

An import cannot recover `credentials`: SELECT returns no credentials on this resource. Put the credentials in your configuration before importing, and the first apply after the import will re-send them — which makes SELECT revalidate the connection against S3.

## Additional Information

### Credentials: a role or an access key

`authentication_method` picks how SELECT signs in, and decides which other fields `credentials` takes. SELECT rejects a field that doesn't belong to the chosen method.

- `role`: SELECT assumes the role in `role_arn`. Its trust policy names SELECT's AWS account, with the external ID shown in SELECT as the `sts:ExternalId` condition. Both values are shown where you add an AWS account in SELECT.
- `access_key`: SELECT signs in with an IAM user's `access_key_id` and `secret_access_key`. They move together, because SELECT has no way to change one without the other.

Either way, the role or user needs to list and read the report objects under `s3_prefix`. SELECT never returns the credentials, so a change made outside Terraform is invisible to a refresh. Terraform re-sends them only when the configured values themselves change.

### Creating a connection validates it against S3

SELECT runs its checks in order before it stores anything: for a role, assuming it; then reaching the bucket, finding a CUR manifest under the prefix, reading the latest manifest, and confirming the export includes the columns SELECT needs. A create that fails leaves no connection behind, and the error names the check that stopped the run along with what to change. A check is only reported as `skipped` when an earlier one already failed.

This means `terraform apply` needs credentials that actually work and a report that has actually been delivered, and that an AWS outage will fail the apply rather than store a broken connection.

There is deliberately no separate credentials check: S3's `HeadBucket` does not reliably distinguish invalid credentials from valid credentials that cannot reach this particular bucket. The failure message carries the AWS error code, so the two are still distinguishable from what SELECT reports.

### Which changes revalidate

SELECT revalidates whenever an apply changes `aws_account_id`, `s3_bucket`, `s3_prefix`, `region` or `credentials`. Changing only `name` or `sync_enabled` makes no call to AWS, so a rename works even when S3 does not.

### Nothing forces a replacement

Every configurable field on this resource can be changed in place, including `aws_account_id` — SELECT moves the connection to the new AWS account and revalidates rather than requiring a new connection. This is unlike the Snowflake, Databricks and BigQuery resources, each of which has at least one field fixed at creation.

### One connection per AWS account, and per report location

SELECT refuses a second connection that would read ground it already covers. Two configurations are rejected:

- an `aws_account_id` that another connection in the organization already reads, and
- an `s3_bucket` and `s3_prefix` pair another connection already reads.

The second is worth calling out separately: two AWS accounts delivering to the same bucket need different prefixes.

### `s3_prefix` is the only field that can be cleared

Removing `s3_prefix` from the configuration moves SELECT to reading the root of the bucket. Every other field rejects removal — an account with no name, no account id, no bucket, no region or no credentials cannot ingest anything, so there is no cleared state for them to have.

An empty string is not the same as no prefix. `s3_prefix = ""` is stored as an empty prefix and counts as a different report location from an absent one when SELECT checks for duplicates. Omit the field rather than setting it to `""`.

### Changes made outside Terraform

Every write carries the connection's `etag` as an `If-Match` header, so an update or delete is refused if the connection changed since Terraform last read it. When that happens, run `terraform apply -refresh-only` to pick up the current state and then apply again.

The ETag also moves when the connection is renamed or when `sync_enabled` is toggled, because both are stored on the underlying connection record. An update revalidates its ETag a second time after the round trip to S3, so a concurrent write that lands mid-request is refused rather than silently overwritten.

### Deleting a connection is not reversible

Destroying this resource removes the connection and the usage data SELECT has collected through it. Re-adding the same AWS account and report location starts its history over.
